label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: 93N conditions
reports.comment:
quick: Took the skis for a walk up Bow Summit to see what conditions are like. 

HS varied from 10-15cm at the trailhead (2100m) to 25-30cm at the upper end of treeline (2300m), deeper where trees have caught wind transported snow, but not by much. 

Poking into the lower alpine we found less snow and soft ~10cm thick windslabs forming. Alpine slopes generally not in for travel by skis yet. 

Spot…

reports.title: dogleg
reports.comment: quick: was going to be an easy day and then we decided to push over to the dogleg and take a look, after finding deeper snow we decided to head up and attempt to ski the dogleg but on coming down we triggered a slab and one skier got taken out by out / avalanche: slab layer that we think formed after the winds from the day before,  it was an isolated pocket on the face / incident: after skier drop…

reports.title: Bow summit ski tour
reports.comment: quick: Didn’t see any avalanches just a few small sluff slides when skiing down steeper sections

reports.title: Bow summit ski resort official opening.
reports.comment:
quick: 30-40cm new snow in parking lot.
Hs of 40-60cm on slope.
Well consolidated first 20 cm of moist snow. With 20-40  of varying storm snow interfaces.
Rocky bowls still look rough.

reports.title: Wapta
reports.comment:
quick: Took a long walk up to Wapta for some early season turns. 

Travel to the hut is as rugged as you might imagine. We were able to keep skis on most of the way but delicate walking was key to not wrecking the skins. 


80cm of snow on the glacier is just enough to totally hide crevasses with week bridges. 120cm was found on the way up Rhondda at about 2900m. Here we had a quick dig. RPs down …

reports.title: Observation
reports.comment: quick: Nice day out. Opted to explore the lower slopes on observation rather than brave the crowds in jimmy jr bowl and bow summit. Snowpack feels very supportive. HS ranges from 40-60cm. Skinning through the trees is fairly gross, wouldn’t follow our track. Ski quality is great and didn’t hit any rocks on mellow open slopes. Temperatures stayed fairly warm. -2 ish. Light winds. Overcast skies. No…

reports.title: Bow summit early season
reports.comment: quick: Skied a few laps Saturday am at bow summit. Lightly clouded and minimal wind - 3c. Pleasantly surprised by the ski quality - 25cm boot pen, no wind effect snow, on a supportive snow pack. Probed 40-70cm depth, right side up, on the main ski slope... Many sharks, but didn't hit any while skiing.

reports.title: Onion cornice failure
reports.comment: avalanche: Ice season is on! While climbing aimless gully this morning we observed a cornice failure on the south aspect of the Onion. There was significant runout reaching near valley bottom.

reports.title: Bow Summit + Dog Leg Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Skied a couple laps of the bowl and chutes of Bow Summit. Boot packed up Dog Leg Couloir. Conditions were great in the morning but due to warmer temperatures conditions decreased to a heavy snow pack throughout the day. 30cm to 70cm in some areas. Some sharks exposed.

reports.title: Bow Summit-Dog Leg Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Rode Dog Leg Couloir from 3/4 of the way up. After seeing reports of a skier incident last week and feeling a more loaded pocket/windslab on the top part of the line, we skipped the last few meters. It was protected from the wind with limited overhead hazard. Though we did see a natural size 1 from an overhead slope right of the Stem couloir. There was warming throughout the day but had lef…

reports.title: Jimmy junior bowl
reports.comment: quick: Great riding conditions! We observed snow depths of 40-50cm, 10cm of fist snow on top of a supportive mid pack. We observed a thin temperature crust 10cm down on the skin track disappearing as we left tree line. Light snow transport.

reports.title: Bow Summit Snow/Wind
reports.comment: quick: Skied Bow Summit on Thursday. Rain as we drove up the parkway but changed to snow around Mosquito Creek. Tons of wet heavy snow at the parking lot and throughout the skin up. Only about -2 in the parking lot. As we broke out of the tree line the snow was lighter and there was a ton of wind. Could see wind lips forming but stayed in the small trees. There was a ton of wind once you got out o…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Warmin up!
reports.comment: quick: No new obsy

reports.title: Dog Leg and Bow Suumit
reports.comment: quick: Bow summit was pretty good skiing this am. Had to be 30 people there. Booted up dog leg couloir to before where people have been turning around and went down due to a 30-40cm deep slab that was quite easy to pull away with hand shears. I dug into the snow in the middle of the fan before heading up and as expected with a previous slide and lots of tracks there was nothing really of note. I t…

reports.title: Bow Summit NE Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Went up to Bow Summit NE Ridge to check out the snowpack, followed our skin track on the way down. Skiing felt supportive and nice turns on fresh snow. Moderate NW winds on the ridge, at tree line wind transport was visible on the surface of the snow. 
At 2350m, HS varied from 70 to 95cm on the ridge. Upper snowpack was about 30cm of F snow, mid pack gradually becoming denser and 10cm of fa…

reports.title: It's on at treeline
reports.comment:
quick: Excellent conditions for skiing at treeline. Supportive base and midpack with 20-30cm of fist on top.

We dug a pit at 2260m in open trees and found HS of 90cm. 26cm of F storm snow over a right side up mid pack and base trending 4F-P. CTH 20 RP compression test results failing at interface between storm snow and old surfaces.

Observed debris from 3 Sz 1 wind slabs on alpine fan features, …

reports.title: Bow Summit - Observation
reports.comment: quick: Breakable crust beneath ~15cm at highway.  Crust disappeared around 2200m.  Stuck with mellow terrain out of the wind and was rewarded with 15~30cm deep turns.

reports.title: Bow Summit Gullies
reports.comment: quick: We rode the gullies and open slope the S.E. of the gullies. No apparent cornices present yet. Friday's storm dropped 15 - 30 cms of snow to ride on.

reports.title: Jimmy junior ski resort
reports.comment:
quick: The ski resort was open for business today, counted 35 people by 11:30 getting after it. 
Supportive crust through tree line, Disappearing at 2000m with up to 4 cm new storm snow filling the old skin track. 15cm ski penetration in the bowl.
There was a stiffer layer in the snow pack about 30cm down in the bowl itself which made for lovely skiing with plenty of fresh stuff still available. 
…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr 500
reports.comment: quick: Solid base with a few good turns of powder in the right places. No signs of instabilities. Still a thin base with rocks hidden just below the surface. Main runs are getting skied out but it's sharky going too far off to the sides.

reports.title: The Snow Shall Be Shallow and You Shall Like It
reports.comment:
quick: Skiied on the lower slopes of Observation Sub Peak today. Good supportive snow below 2200m, made the tree-bashing the way up a little less bad. HS increased gradually to avg 60cms above treeline, then decreased as we approached steeper and more wind-affected slopes. Stopped climbing at 2520m and decided to ski.

Pit digging at this time resulted in CTE9 down 12 SP, reacting in the RGxf inte…

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak North Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Poked around the alpine across the street from the Jimmy Junior/Bow Summit festival. Supportive snowpack to 60cm up to treeline making for pretty easy access to the alipine. Once above TL, very variable snow depths. 

Somehow we managed to not hit any rocks staying in the thickest concavities in the moraines - depths varying from 0 to 1m, very quick thick-to-thin transitions. Evidence of su…

reports.title: Wet and Wild Crystal Healing
reports.comment:
quick: Skiied up Crystal Ridge today. Supportive base provides lovely skinning up to alpine, approaching 70cm HS at TL, and then reducing in the wind-affected Alpine. HS was highly variable, however 60cms of moist, consolidated snow provides good skiing in protected lees. 

Dug a pit, snowpack is moist to ground at 2350m on solar aspects. Compression Tests repeatedly failed on isolation at ground.…

reports.title: Observation
reports.comment: quick: -12C at start.  Frozen tree bombs.  The crust did not disappear even at 2700m except for low/zero solar aspects.  Travel was good.  Descent was a balance of depth of cover (low solar) vs crust (at least some solar).  The bushwhack to the road had good snow when dark.

reports.title: Observation peak area
reports.comment: quick: Went up to the summit of observation then skied down the SE chute and out on the lower slopes. Windslabs building in the alpine with steady moderate winds gusting into strong. The gut of the chute we skied slid naturally in the last 12hrs. Saw surface hoar growth at TL on the approach that should get blown away. Of note we saw 4 size 1 slides on glacier ice on the observation North glacier …

reports.title: GD
reports.comment:
quick: Topped out on Grand daddy today the  cornice was an acceptable size to move the group up through the over head. 
Through the couloir the snow was pretty consolidated hand sheers were very stubborn. FP was usually around 10-15 cm so made for reasonable travel . 
Light to moderate winds at ridge top with some blowing snow and sluff coming off the walls. 
The fan had a supportive crust with 5-…

reports.title: The MINfluence begins…
reports.comment:
quick: Bow summit day. Skied several features. Most treeline and below slopes had been heavily tracked with some minor overnight refill and we saw no signs of instability.

Up the stem the choke was very thin and firm after being schralped by several parties yesterday(very marginal for skiing) but the rest skied ok. The petals were also thin with steady moderate wind transport at ridgetop. We turn…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr. Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Generally decent skiing on 5-15 cm powder or  soft wind slab on the crust.  There was a size 1 to 1.5 natural wind slab avalanche that pulled out of a N pocket at 2550m see photos. Obsevered Mid morning.  The crown looked 30 to 50cm deep.

reports.title: Bow Summit Area alpine
reports.comment: quick: Poked around in the bow summit alpine area. Started booting up upper dog leg and turned around. Maybe it had a track in it. Could have been a spindrift runnel too. Didn’t like the 35-50cm windslab. Booted up some other obscure features. The windslabs vary from 15cm formed recently to 50cm that was formed during the last storm and that hasn’t seen tracks. Winds were westerlies when we arrive…

reports.title: Dogleg Saturday Morning
reports.comment: quick: Skied Dogleg again above bow summit. On the boot pack up the top 5ish cm was not bonding well at the start which increased to 10cm higher up. Prob ~10cm overnight since we were in there yesterday. On the ski down from the top I popped the top 15cm across 2/3 of the width of the feature. Snow increased noticeably around 11am with more spin drifting off the walls around. A group of 4 was in t…

reports.title: Observation Sub-Peak Supreme
reports.comment: quick: SW and S aspects were quite wind-affected and shallow with rocks poking through but SE aspect was supreme. Lots of powder without any signs of instability. The ski-out is not for beginners with tight trees and some bushwacking. 70cm snow depth at treeline on southeastern aspect.

reports.title: Japow, Icefields Parkway
reports.comment:
quick: Skiing in Japow today, too much snow, we saw and heard multiple size 1.5-3 avalanche in very steep terrain mostly east facing and some recent debris nearby.

The weather cleared up nicely for about an hour in the morning and even some sun. That quickly turned into heavy snowfall and some near white outs for the rest of our day. >15cm of fresh snow from the last couple of days made breaking …

reports.title: Dolomite area
reports.comment: quick: Measured as little as 20cm of snow and as much as 100cm of snow in varying spots. Snow was quite slow for skiing. Triggered sluffs on steeper short slopes that could have  turned into something bigger on a bigger slope.

reports.title: Crystal Ridge Road Side
reports.comment: quick: Great riding conditions in the trees on Crystal Ridge. We saw no signs of instability in the trees. Did see some areas where the creek was open.

reports.title: Bow Summit Viewpoint
reports.comment: quick: Skinned up to just below the Bow summit viewpoint and skied the lower slopes in the glades below the tree line. We started around 9am, it was quite cloudy and windy with poor visibility until around 11, when the clouds parted and made for a beautiful ride down with deep pow and perfect visibility. Measured about 130-140cm of snow to the base. Snow pack felt quite stable and didn’t see or he…

reports.title: Jimmy Junior Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Slopes leading to Jimmy Junior peak were thin, HS 10-40cm - this area seemed to have wind affect from the previous storm. A thin temperature crust existed on most of the Southern Half above 2400m. 

Jimmy Junior bowl had 10-30cm of dry snow,  HS of 40-80cm and skiing very well. A small size 1 Sst was noticed at 2500m, SE asp, crown looks between 20-40cm deep. Picture attached. 
No slab qual…

reports.title: Jimmy Junior Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Slopes leading to Jimmy Junior peak were thin, HS 10-40cm - this area seemed to have wind affect from the previous storm. A thin temperature crust existed on most of the Southern Half above 2400m. 

Jimmy Junior bowl had 10-30cm of dry snow,  HS of 40-80cm and skiing very well. A small size 1 Sst was noticed at 2500m, SE asp, crown looks between 20-40cm deep. Picture attached. 
No slab qual…

reports.title: Dolomite Area
reports.comment: quick: Skied lines across from Dolomite Peak. Coverage varied from 30cm to over 100cm in areas. Access is well filled in and protected lines hold great skiing with no rocks poking through. Exiting the area on more wind exposed areas still had plenty of sharks to be found.

reports.title: Grand Daddy
reports.comment: quick: Just a heads up that the cornice on the Grand Daddy Couloir on Bow Peak is fairly large and very overhanging. It does not appear this way from below but is quite threatening when observed from the side. The cornice itself is quite easy to climb around and the terrain provides fairly straightforward access to the ridge, but it would be catastrophic if that thing fell with people below it.

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment:
quick: 10 AM start - no wind - sunny sky’s with a -10 C.

River crossing not filled in.  Tippy toed across a section to the north with skis on.  Thankfully held.

12 “ of fresh well bonded and settled.  No wind impact to the tree line of West Nile.  Couldn’t see well enough into Alpine but wind loading looked negligible.  No evidence of any instability at tree-line or any alpine.

Probed 80-100 cm…

reports.title: Dolomite Circuit
reports.comment: quick: Skied the Dolomite Circuit to take advantage of the sunny day. There is enough coverage for access but it is still thin enough to present some challenges. Some wind affect is starting to appear especially on Northern and Eastern aspects that was not present when I was in the area on the 26th. Sheltered areas still holding very good powder but the skiing down from the pass and out were very …

reports.title: Cirque
reports.comment: quick: Supportive crust made travel below treeline manageable. At treeline there was 10-15 cm of powder on top of the crust, which made for great skiing and kept you above the worst of the hazards. There was surface hoar developing in the morning, but  we could see the crystals melting throughout the day. Transitioning without gloves and skinning in a t-shirt, so likely near 0. Most of the snow in…

reports.title: Jimothy jr fun times
reports.comment:
quick: Jimmy jr starting to get tracked out but still some lines to be had. Snow was about 65 cm deep in the two places we probed. About 15 people out today. Snow felt good, no signs of instability, there’s about 10 cm of pow above a firmer, faster layer. 

Fun times.

reports.title: Observation Subpeak alpine
reports.comment:
quick: Managed to skin 95% of the way to the summit with only moderate disregard for equipment. 

North glacier skied well despite a bit of wind crust here and there. Probed 90-110cm.

Exited out the south bowl feature from just below the summit. First pitch skied great, lower parts were thin, rocky, and wind affected.

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Generally poor coverage on the highway side of crystal ridge, but we found pockets of good riding on mellow slopes. Skin track was steep in spots, punched out and getting slick. Not a single wind slab was found. Needs more snow and time!

reports.title: Crowfoot Couloir & Pow Laps
reports.comment:
quick: Skiied crowfoot couloir and then did some laps in the area. Wind was picking up, lots of spindrift pouring off the headwall throughout the day. Pockets of wind slab were starting to take shape up high, but not enough to cause us issue. Couloir was variable but mostly hard, and has seen considerable natural sluffing. 

The rest of the riding was excellent. Snow depth still highly variable fr…

reports.title: Solved the Puzzle
reports.comment:
quick: MINfluencer back at it again. Collabed with IanMach10 to ski the lesser known Puzzle Peak Couloir.

Travel up to dolomite shoulder/puzzle ramp was well tracked and easy in the trees. Travel became more variable in wind exposed terrain where snow depths ranged from 1m to 20cm. Deeper spots were dense and right side up.

Top of the couloir we found a 10cm soft wind slab isolated to the immedi…

reports.title: Observation peak area
reports.comment:
quick: We skied a south facing slope near observation peak and found some great turns with soft snow on top of a supportive base. The recent winds deposited a lot of new snow where we skied, and we didnt notice any slabs except for on some more SE facing slopes we briefly travelled on during the skin up.
A lot of the alpine terrain is pretty thin right now with the recent winds, and there are some…

reports.title: Observation observations
reports.comment:
quick: We skied west and southwest aspects off of Observation subpeak. Variable crusty and wind affected snow made for hooky skiing in the alpine. Ok snow found at treeline and in mellow sheltered terrain. 

Found breakable suncrust down ~5-10cm on solar alpine and treeline slopes and noticed surface snow becoming moist and rollerballing in the afternoon. Broken skies with light-moderate W/NW wind…

reports.title: Crystal ridge backside
reports.comment: quick: Did a lap of the sitting bull next to sugar cube couloir. Decent conditions on lee slopes, definitely still rocky though. Folks skied the sugar cube, with many rocks on exit. Minor surface wind slab with limited energy. Exited via Helen’s Shoulder bowl, which is absolutely horrendous and rocky. Needs a lot more snow.

reports.title: Hope you like rocks bands and micro gullies.
reports.comment:
quick: Light snow drifting in with light wind, 
We noticed variety of snows. Very thin in spots. 

Navigating very shallow rock bands to find better skiing. 

Lots of wind effect, found small pockets of leeward wind slabs. Able to produce small pocket slabs, sliding on some surface hoar. 

Propagating around d 10ish metres, crowns of 10ish cms. 

Early season conditions will funnel you into small …

reports.title: Cirque peak west face
reports.comment: quick: Good snow quality at tree line. We did not notice any instability and no signs of natural activity. We did see some isolated wind affect snow.

reports.title: Sugar Cube
reports.comment:
quick: Skied sugar cube couloir.

Appproached up and over crystal ridge. We found 3cm of new snow on the skin track in the trees, and 20-30cm of ski penetration trail breaking above tree line. We managed to skin to within 20m of the ridgetop before being forced to take our skis off and bootpack due to lack of snow on the ridge. Some of the lower sections of crystal ridge frontside looked like good…

reports.title: Crowfoot Cruisin
reports.comment: quick: Great riding and travel conditions today in the Crowfoot glades zone. Numerous parties out (at least 4 we saw), and every group had some great turns. The mid pack crust was still very supportive and provided great skiing conditions, limiting any shark attacks (none). Enjoyable riding conditions! Lake is frozen with a layer of snow over the top, as we were heading back noticed some deeper po…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Went for a poke around Crowfoot after yesterday’s storm. Thankfully a track had been set yesterday - boot deep travel today in the skin track, knee to thigh deep otherwise. 

Rode two gullies - first was almost too mellow to ride with the amount of snow, the second much steeper, with incredible unconsolidated pow. Some minor sloughing but nothing of worry. No signs of instabilities. 

Lake …

reports.title: Cristal Ridge tree line
reports.comment: quick: Stayed below tree line. 50+ cm fresh powder snow. Lot of rocks hidden on steeper terrain. Whoumfs sound heard near the tree line.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: The avalanche forecast was at Level 4/High, so we skinned in on the summer trail to the first saddle, dug a pit in a sheltered area at treeline and skied out through the trees.  No open slopes or open trees.  Out ECT result was ECT18N@50.  Other than that, we observed no other signs of instability. / weather: intermittent light snow, becoming heavier as the afternoon progressed. Ground leve…

reports.title: Soft snow in crowfoot
reports.comment:
quick: Tons of great fresh snow in crowfoot. On steeper north facing terrain dug a quick pit and found HS 135, and failure CT16 on the old snow interface down 55cm, 20° slope at 2200 above the cliffy pillow terrain. 

Kept out of the steeper stuff and wiggled through the trees.

reports.title: Struggle fest for powder turns
reports.comment:
quick: Travel below treeline pretty rugged, approach was still pretty thin with lots of exposed logs, etc.  Noticed a recent size 1 slab in steep terrain while skinning up.

Enjoyed some mellow slopes in gladed terrain.  In the alpine, conditions looked pretty rocky so we stayed below treeline. 

Third skiier across popped a 5 metre long slab to the Nov 22 crust traversing across a wind loaded con…

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Skiied Crystal Ridge and Helen Shoulder.
HS at Crystal varied from 110 to rocky and marginal.
Helen Shoulder had good powder on some sheltered east aspects and slab with 20 m shooting cracks on wind exposed slopes.

reports.title: Dolomite ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Good day for walking around in deep snow.
Temps hovered around -1 most of the day with around 5-10 cm or moist snow from the day.
Dug on a SE slope finding our layer of concern 50cm down. CTV sp on a layer of 4f facets.

reports.title: Crowfoot chutes area
reports.comment:
quick: We skied the crowfoot chutes area and a couple of groups in the area. The skin track moves quickly and was fairly beaten in. We did some random probes and found an average snow depth of ~200cm. The snow seemed to be bonding quite well and we skied a steeper chute with no evidence of instability on the skin up or the ski down apart from sluffing.

We saw some trees shedding snow throughout t…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Skied out what remains of the crowfoot glades, there’s not much that isn’t tracked out unless you’re willing to get creative. Noticed windslabs but none thicker than 15 cm.

reports.title: Bring a shovel for your car
reports.comment: quick: Crowfoot glades are skiing well, and if you’re willing there are still lots of good times to be had! We noticed some soft slabs in the new snow on convex rolls, but nothing that worried us. Saw some folks putting ski tracks into the alpine as well. On our way back to the car we saw a size 2 natural releasing from Central Crowfoot but our viewpoint didn’t allow us to see whether the impact s…

reports.title: A puzzle of wind slab, crust and powder
reports.comment: quick: Went for a ski up Puzzle Peak Ramp.  New snow made for easy travel below treeline.  The ramp was a mix of wind affected snow with some localized windslab, crust and powder, alternating between sunny skies and howling wind.  Hollow sounding snow at one point on uptrack, and evidence of a Size 2 dry loose avalanche in steep terrain off Oxo peak, likely from earlier this week.  We found a powd…

reports.title: Bow Summit area
reports.comment: weather: Strong winds & downdrafts, along with a very warm (for the Rockies) afternoon made for a blustery day.  Extensive snow plumes at treeline & above.  Cornices still small & tender, / snowpack: Compression test  result with 28 taps, with a sudden planar break.  A thin layer of partially decomposed dendrites appeared to be the failure layer, with a 4 finger (resistance) slab above, and 1 fing…

reports.title: Bow Hut area
reports.comment:
quick: Bow Hut - Jan 10-11, 2026. Broke trail from the parking lot all the way to the hut yesterday. Extreme winds, lots of blowing snow all over. Some alpine slopes are looking very wind stripped. 
Coverage was excellent for this time of year. The canyon was pretty straightforward considering. We did not find any reactive wind slabs despite finding a lot of wind affected snow all over. No natural…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr N paths
reports.comment:
quick: Alpine Air Adventures AST 2 students and guides observations, day 1 discovery day. 

CTM (15) x 2 down 45 cm on Jan 3rd well preserved SH 3-5mm, sudden planner results on 25 deg slope at 2000M

ECTN (15), minimal propagation BUT when block pulled it slid off clean and fast.

RB 3 at same site on Jan 3rd SH

Snowpack depth 180-200cm, midpack is well settled. / snowpack: Alpine Air Adventures…

reports.title: Observation subpeak
reports.comment:
quick: Moderate NW winds with alpine high -5.  

Winds in the Bow Summit area kept the snow dryer over the last couple days than the Pulpits.  Didn't find much sun crust but lots of wind affect in the alpine.  Found short pitches of good snow on the lower south slopes of Observation subpeak and  NE  trees of Crystal ridge.

Had a look at skiing the north glacier of observation subpeak but looked t…

reports.title: Icefields Parkway Conditions
reports.comment:
quick: With mild temps, light inversions and clear skies, spent the last couple days enjoying the alpine views along the icefields parkway.

We skied Mt Rhonda above the Wapta icefields on Friday, and Observation Subpeak Thursday. Evidence of an avalanche cycle from the warmup last week, old debris to size 2 on lee aspects, mostly looking to have been started by cornice failure pulling slabs on st…

reports.title: Sunny Skies on St.Nick
reports.comment:
quick: Toured up to St.Nick from bow lake. 

After reaching the summit we down climbed to just below and skied an NEE aspect down. 
Skiing conditions were breakable hard pressed wind affect. 

Pockets of wind slab were coming off with hard hand shears although no major results or propagation on the ski down. 

On the glacier conditions were hard pressed textured wind affect supportive to skier tra…

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment: quick: Rode north facing slopes in the crowfoot glades area. Alpine basin was wind affected, snow was firm and the skiing was sub par. Once in the north facing trees there was no wind affect or crust and the riding quality was fantastic. Saw signs of point releases from that day on sunny south-facing slopes across the valley. Temperatures wildly fluctuating based on aspect and sun exposure.

reports.title: Grand Daddy
reports.comment:
quick: Skiied up to the base of GD Couloir. -10c at the car, but felt much warmer higher up and in the sun. 
Opted not to ski the Couloir since we witnessed large blocks of snow come tumbling down from above during our approach (presumably from the sunny faces above), and it being warmer than expected. 
The fan was a mix of rock hard avi debris and grabby wind crust (up to 4cm). The couloir didnt …

reports.title: Mt Weed South face
reports.comment: quick: Skied Mt Weed S face today. Excellent travel through the treeline. Supportive snowpack with soft snow in top. No temp crust. Into alpine wind has consolidated the pack well too making for great travel. A few cm's of soft on top for good ski quality. High alpine has taken a pretty good beating from the wind but made for good booting. Some thin areas have sluffed to ground from solar and a fa…

reports.title: Jimmy Junior Summit
reports.comment: quick: Cautiously investigated the classic SE face of Jimmy Junior, finding evidence of the previously reported cornice-triggered Sz 2 slide. Skinning this bedding surface then booting through rocks to avoid a loaded section gave access to the upper face which was heavily wind affected as expected (ski crampons required). After a short, rocky bootpack to the summit, we found surprisingly enjoyable…

reports.title: Crowfoot Couloir
reports.comment: quick: We dog a pit and got ECTP15 at  125cm of the 150cm snowpack. There is definitely a crust on the top of the pack too as you can see on the picture.

reports.title: No mosquitos but pow fever
reports.comment: quick: Went out for some powder laps in the West Nile slide paths with ACC Calgary BITS.  Skin track up through the trees in good shape with a few icy sections.  Avalanche paths were in great shape with powder most of the way down, except for some wind affected near the top.  Noticed some loose dry in steep terrain off Bow Peak Clifs above the bench at the end of the day which we hadn't seen in th…

reports.title: Crowfoot Mountain
reports.comment: quick: Good travel on the lake and through the canyon. A few very small slides running to the skin track which appear to be several days old, no recent activity. Skin track to the glacier is icy, 0cm ski pen off track, several places in the trees where crampons would've been nice. Easy travel though the moraines, good coverage on the glacier, probed 280cm. Slopes leading to the summit are very win…

reports.title: Crowfoot Moraines
reports.comment: snowpack: Two profiles in Crowfoot Moraines, one in the trees and one on a moraine wall, both clearly showed the January 3 surface hoar layer down 50 and 60 cm with sudden planar compression test results.

reports.title: Gordon NW Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Good quick travel. Snow depths on the glacier were 2-300cm of consistant Pencil to the ice. Very few obvious sags. Started the day out with the rope on to feel it out but removed it early on for the rest of the day. Felt Low Low Low with high confidence. Skied wind effected areas. convexities and areas of thick to thin with no signs of instibility. / snowpack: Supportive wind crust skied co…

reports.title: St. Nicholas
reports.comment: quick: Great day up on the wapta, seeing great skinning conditions and boot packing conditions up to st. Nic. Travel through bow lake up the headwall was relatively relaxed with pockets of Isolated mostly unsupportive windslab in immediate Lee's coming out of the creek and up to bow hut. No major instability noted. On the glacier itself Seeing good coverage with good travel on wind scoured surface…

reports.title: Gordon
reports.comment:
quick: 8:00am start from the car park air temp was around -16, S-1 along the lake and up through the canyon travel was not too bad. 

Through the canyon SH buried 1-2 cm 1-3 mm, under 2 cm of new fist snow. 
2150m 2 cm F , overlying a 4f + thin breakable crust beginning to facet with mainly facets below but I didn’t stop to dig too much in tree line. 

Up on the glacier at about 1030 we were bless…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: We skied at Bow Summit and dug both a CT and a ETC. The snowpack was 180cm. We got CTV2 at 160cm. We then got ECTP2 at 160cm. 

The snowpack below seems well consolidated, except when we pulled the column with our shovel for fun after the test, we got a planar failure at 100cm. It seems however very hard to trigger it. 

Fun day outside.

reports.title: V A R I A B L E (Jimmy Jr. Bowl)
reports.comment: quick: Group of 2 headed up for a couple of laps in Jimmy Jr. bowl. Encountered 2 other parties of 2 in the area. Light snowfall and moderate winds in the alpine were transporting snow into the bowl. Not enough to be concerned but definitely something to watch out for in the coming days if the wind keeps up. Bowl was wind affected and every turn/step was different. We observed crusts of varying th…

reports.title: Remote triggered windslab @bow
reports.comment: incident: Remote triggered while skinning across an alpine slope just north of granddaddy couloir. One caught and taken for a ride ~15-20m. Trigger point was over some buried rocks that can be seen under the crown in the photos. Very large chunks in the slide.

reports.title: Lookers left of Sugar cube
reports.comment:
avalanche: Lookers left of sugar cube. ski cut a cross loaded part of the slope, triggered a loose dry that was 1ft-1inch at the crown.

No other instability noted.

reports.title: Crampons, ice axe and face shots
reports.comment:
quick: Went for a ski tour up Jimmy Junior Peak.  Travel below treeline was fairly smoothe with some crusty sections.  Ski crampons were very helpful for steep rising traverse above the bench.  Brought boot crampons in case needed for the summit but didn't need them, but found the ice axe helpful.  

Snow quality at the top of the run was amazing with surfy pow turns, turning more crusty lower dow…

reports.title: Patterson
reports.comment:
quick: Skied to the ridge of Patterson. Lots of evidence of wet slides from the warm spell last week in the canyon. We also triggered a 3x3 meter 10cm slab in the canyon without consequence.
Wind affected crusty powder above the creek. Did not summit up wind blasted scree to summit.

reports.title: Sugar cube couloir
reports.comment:
quick: We booted up. Snow was hard and wind scoured. Higher up in the couloir a wind crust was developing and kept getting thicker with sugary weak snow underneath.

Not good skiing, iffy conditions. Not worth it.

reports.title: Bow Summit Ski Tour!
reports.comment: quick: A few inches of light and fluffy snow! Overall great conditions considering how little snow we have had lately. As you got further up snow was getting a bit crusty. Stayed away from rocky areas where the snowpack transitioned from thick to thin.

reports.title: Sneaky Good Skiing
reports.comment:
quick: Beauty day at Bow Summit today. ~8-10cm of fresh snow, clear skies and low winds made for a great day of skiing from treeline down. Conditions were quite fantastic and “buttery” for how little snow we have received recently. 

Ridgeline/benches were wind blasted and hard but not bulletproof. We entered all slopes below ridgeline as we were conscious of windslabs. 

By 1pm snow was beginning…

reports.title: Bow Lake/Crowfoot Mtn
reports.comment:
quick: We dug a pit at the treeline.  Findings were very consistent with forecast for the day. Thin, but very dense wind slab for top 5 cm (pencil).  Under that, 1 finger for 60 cm, becoming more cohesive as we went down.

The picture is of a sudden planar activation CTH 30 at 60 cm.  Very smooth plane. No clearly visible hoar or facets at that level.  These were hard hits.  Beneath that there was…

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak West Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Warm wet and sticky snow from the car to ~2300m. Travel improved significantly on wind affected surfaces at tree line and above. Very strong gusts of wind out of the NE with significant snow transport in the alpine. Turned around at ridgeline due to wind. Ski down was mix of crusts,  sastrugi, and dust on crust in the alpine, with soft snow at TL that got wetter as we descended.

reports.title: I like my skiing like I like my handshakes…
reports.comment:
quick: Firm.

Observation sub peak north glacier and couloir skied either smooth knife boilerplate windslab/suncrust or pencil sastrugi. 

Skinning was tough up any wind or sun exposed slopes with 0cm ski pen much of the way.

Surface snow on southwest aspects was moist down 5-10cm by 2pm with occasional size one wet loose entraining off the ski. Decent corn skiing for February. 

Minor wind trans…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glade
reports.comment:
quick: AST2 group with UCalgary Outdoor Centre / snowpack: HS185, and dug 135cm at W aspect, 18 degrees concave.  CT1 RP down 7cm (WD), with second failure CT19 RP down 22cm on the Jan 24th melt crust. 

4F down 35cm; 1F down 35-95cm; P below. Didn't probe K layer. Observed cornice failure off ridge west of where we were (The mountain south of North Crowfoot Mountain), estimate size 2

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment: quick: Party of 4 went for a tour up into Crowfoot glades. Saw two other large parties in the area. Heavy wind affect seen in area. Snow was variable and ranged from firm powder to bulletproof crust. We skinned up through the valley and gained the bench for some views then skied down through the trees and into the drainage. The best snow was definitely in the sheltered tree areas where the wind di…

reports.title: Crowfoot Mountain
reports.comment: quick: Mostly thin crust, but powder on higher slopes. Size 2 avalanche seen from a distance, likely from an above cornice.

reports.title: Mt Patterson access
reports.comment:
quick: Explored the Patterson access route through delta creek.

Good
Travel up to the canyon was fast and supportive 
Bad
Poor ski quality breakable crusts, on exit and a avalanche fan we poked around
Ugly
The boot pack up the canyon was variable( some bullet proof, some wind crusts, some facet to ground and no clues on the surface)
After the 1st section the traverse was wind hammered not easy to…

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment:
quick: -18 at the car @ 8am and -2 at 12.30. 
very cold moderate winds in the valley early on but calm once up high. 
fast travel from top to bottom yesterday with great travel through the canyon and mostly hard conditions above treeline. 
glacier coverage mostly good. ~80cms at the toe increasing to an average of ~240 higher up. 
and some soft blown in powder for the way down. 
luge track on the …

reports.title: Cirque lake
reports.comment:
quick: Attempted cirque to chephren lake traverse today( guild book say mistaya traverse)

Crossed at waterfowl out flow no concerns 
Travel through the trees was rugged, but supportive, lot of tree rain.(make sure you ski edges are sharp)
Travel in the open fens and areas with no tree canopy has 1cm of fresh convective snow, with a sun crust underneath( thickness depends on how much sun it’s gets…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Observed a natural size 2 coming down the gully right in the center of the picture. Visibility was poor, but we could see a subtle debris outline with the naked eye.

reports.title: sugar cube
reports.comment: quick: skied the sugar cube, quality skiing on the feature, soft chalky to dust of crust on the fan. we skied some solar slopes on the way back to the car with ski quality going from bullet proof sun crust to some sweet corn harvesting around 2400m.

reports.title: Crystal Ridge & Cirque N.
reports.comment: quick: Skied the backside of Crystal Ridge & the Cirque N Couloir. The alpine is generally wind hammered, though more sheltered polar aspects had 10cm of 4F making for decent skiing. No evidence of new wind slab in the areas travelled. Currently a 40m rap gets you to the snow in the couloir.

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Headed out to Crystal Ridge, following summer trail. Some trail making needed as not an obvious path but followed the general upward track before breaking out of treeline. Saw some skiers above us, but not busy at all. Snow coming down around Bow Lake made for some great powder turns and sun came out for a great day on the parkway! Some clear avalanche terrain on way up but skied nothing mo…

reports.title: Flower Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Rode the stem today. There was about 10 cm fresh on top of hardpack, which made for a good boot pack. Bit of sluff occurred down the couloir. Conditions were more slab like near the top of the stem. Visibility into the petals was minimal so we did not venture further.

reports.title: Bow Lake Area
reports.comment: quick: Spent most of the day in a blizzard, with flat light and near whiteout conditions. Sun poked through once or twice. Snowed 15-20cm over a crust, made for great skiing, but a lot of slough coming off of the upper cliffs and the steeper slopes had some skier tiggerable dry loose that didn't propagate anywhere. Overall a great day!

reports.title: Refreshing!
reports.comment: quick: Party of two skinned up to crowfoot glades. Saw parties up in the glades, and saw several skiers in the bowl above the moraine. Today was sunny with moderate wind and strong gusts up in the alpine. Enjoyed 15-20 cm of fresh snow that made for excellent skiing in the glades. Due to the cooler temps the snow was soft and light (fist). Did not see any signs of instability where we skied. Heard…

reports.title: OXO / Puzzle Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Dust on crust on the face, as we expected but decided on a walk anyway. Ski crampons might have made the final push to the top easier, but it was workable without them as long as extra effort was put in to establish the skin track. Highly recommend some sharp edges for this one, there's no breaking through that crust. 

I was surprised that the top 2-5cm of powder sitting on the crust wasn'…

reports.title: Dolo(mite) Goody and Hitch
reports.comment: quick: A lovely Dolomite Shoulder day to taste the sun. Mostly wind-smashed snow-on-crust, very directional, very cream cheesy. One crack seen/heard on the skin up, about halfway. Stuck to a very mellow descent.

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment: quick: Good day on Cirque Forepeak. Hard and wind affected up high, but lots of fresh snow lower down in the open glades.

reports.title: Crusty Helen
reports.comment: quick: Great day on Helen Ridge with marginal skiing conditions with about 5-10cm over a supportive crust. Skied the burnt trees in the bowl, a few other groups chose bigger lines up by sitting bull. Alpine was wind blasted, conditions were better in the glades but still crusty. The bottom 1/4 of the ski out was not great- sketchy survival skiing. Helen Lake trailhead is probably a better move for…

reports.title: Dolomite traverse+Cirque N
reports.comment: quick: Skied from Mosquito Cr-Observation sub peak drainage via the Dolomite traverse route + Cirque N couloir after bailing on our original plan due to overnight winds. Overall cloudy day with pockets of sun in the morning. Winds picked up in the afternoon mostly Mod with gusts into strong. Snowing lightly all morning and picking up around 2pm. We covered a lot of terrain and had decent vis. Saw …

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment:
quick: Plan A was to go to Bow Peak but we bailed on it when we saw the conditions on the Parkway and headed to Crowfoot glades.

-6°C at the car at 10am.

30cm+ of new snow in this area with really strong winds and a lot of snow transport, first in the alpine and later down to the valley bottom and the road. Lots of natural avalanches and sluffs around all morning. 

We could see all the summits …

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment:
quick: Plan A was to go to Bow Peak but we bailed on it when we saw the conditions on the Parkway and headed to Crowfoot glades.

-6°C at the car at 10am.

30cm+ of new snow in this area with really strong winds and a lot of snow transport, first in the alpine and later down to the valley bottom and the road. Lots of natural avalanches and sluffs around all morning. 

We could see all the summits …

reports.title: Fat pow
reports.comment:
quick: Skied crowfoot glades. 10-15 cms in the parking lot at 9 am. Mostly light winds/warm and S1. Forecasted winds did not pick up until 3 pm. No signs of instability in the trees. Avg 45-50 cms of fist snow on supportive. 

Heard numerous audible avalanches that lasted 30 seconds plus (suspected cornice triggered windslab coming off headwall of crowfoot.) 

Skiing was almost to deep for angle o…

reports.title: Peyto
reports.comment: quick: Attempted to get to peyto hut. Powder was too deep and hindered approach. The next day was beautiful blue skys. Didn’t get to ski anything. Just skinned down the moraine and out.

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment:
quick: Wind-affected snow In the alpine
Sunny enough to cause some solar warming

reports.title: AST Field day
reports.comment: quick: -17 in Lake Louise, -5 at Bow Summit, +5 at 15:00, Strong SW to W winds starting at noon. 30 cm low density on crust layer. CT12 SP down 30; facet layer at 50 cm. Solar aspect, BTL. Lots of sign of wind slab avalanche activity up to size 2.5 on Lee and cross loaded slopes. 1 settlement BTL. Peyto Lake Lookout road not plowed but plow parked at Crowfoot lookout at end of day is making its wa…

reports.title: Hwy 93N Avalanche Observations March 2
reports.comment: avalanche: Avalanche Observations from a road patrol to Hwy 93N. Evidence of the avalanche cycle last week from sz 2 to sz 3. Most activity was on E aspects however there were notable events on every aspect. Some events clearly involved only storm snow while many others displayed impressive propagation indicative of a persistent slab, particularly near treeline. All events are at least 24hrs old w…

reports.title: Bow Summit conditions
reports.comment:
quick: Skied open trees and gullies below the Bow Summit viewpoint. We counted on heavy ski compaction to have broken up the Jan 24 surface hoar on these slopes. Found good settled powder conditions in sheltered treeline, anywhere exposed to wind was hooky and unpleasant to ski, though we didn't step out into the alpine. 

Saw a number of old crowns above Bow Summit to size 2, noted a size 1.5 tri…

reports.title: Dolomite Traverse conditions
reports.comment: quick: Travel on south and west aspects was crusty, while north and east were wind affected, but we did find some decent turns off the high col. After observing some whumpfing and settling as we descended a NE slope toward Lake Katherine, we decided against doing yo-yos.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the glades today. It was around 0 degrees at the cars, -2 at the top of the runs. Snowed all day with low visibility. 
Wet, heavy and sticky snow throughout the trees. 
We stayed in the trees on mellow slopes. Witnessed two natural avalanches off BowCrow, so stayed away from any overhead hazards. 
Still lots of good skiing if you stick in the trees.
Lake/creek at north end is open, bu…

reports.title: Solid pack with deep powder in glades
reports.comment: quick: Crusty and wind affected on alpine slopes, mid and lower slopes among trees had deep powder. Solid pack, no slabbing or whumphing. About 18cm fresh powder where it didn't blow away.

reports.title: Peyto Moraine
reports.comment: quick: Attempted to get in to peyto hut but turned at the moraine. Had one wumph while gaining the moraine from creek bottom and then remote triggered a 1.5-2 from 60M away (First Photo shows skin track). Failure on the persistent slab varying from 20-50cm thick. 2 other size 1.5-2 spotted from presumably yesterday or overnight (second photo), both looked to have failed on the persistent as well b…

reports.title: We’re so back!
reports.comment: quick: Skied the lookers left avalanche paths on bow peak. Everything below 2000m had a crust underneath the storm snow. Above 2000m it was perfect skiing. We didn’t reach all the way up to the head wall because of whiteout conditions in the morning. However we got to the top of TL and there was no recent wind effect. Dug down to check out the PS which while still visible seemed well bonded and pr…

reports.title: Saw a slide
reports.comment: avalanche: Witness a big slide from a cornice, we viewed the slide from bow hut across the bowl.

reports.title: Saw a slide
reports.comment: avalanche: Witness a big slide from a cornice, we viewed the slide from bow hut across the bowl.

reports.title: PWL result
reports.comment:
snowpack: ECT 29 down 95 sudden planar on .5mm FC expect Jan 24 PWL.

Brent Peters
Mountain Guide
PeakSTRATAGEM.com

reports.title: Peyto-Bow 3 Day Trip
reports.comment: quick: Peyto Hut March 11-13. Observed remote triggers on approach as reported by prior party, we picked a line through a treed shoulder to the rocks to ascend Peyto moraine, but did not feel comfortable returning via this route so exited Bow. Day 1-2 was snowy and storming, wide-spread wind affect. Day 3 cleared and we observed a moderate natural cycle beginning with assumed propagation on the pe…

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: snowpack: Our group dug a pit and did CT and ECT on 30 degree slope. No result on either test (ECTX). In examining the snowpack, we found a layer down 44 cm and another down 85 cm. The latter fractured on a hard shovel shear, on what appeared to be faceted snow; possibly 24 Jan crust.

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl & West Bow Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Skied a line in Jimmy Jr. Bowl. Snow quality is great. Pretty tracked out by now.

Climbed up the trees to end up at the West Bow Peak slide paths. Dug a pit (on pin location) the PS was down 100cm. CTN, ECTX and the interface at the PWL when forcing the column off was non planar and seemed to have slowly started bonding.

Ski quality on West Bow Peak was also fantastic. Light wind effect i…

reports.title: OXO summit day
reports.comment:
quick: 10-15cm of new snow sliding on top of wind affected snow on steep slopes (top pitch). Snow was getting better the more we got down the slope. 

Day was cold in the morning and changed to really hot when the sun came out directly affecting the sunny slopes with heavy radiation (11h30am to 15h30).

We saw many skiers coming from dolomite trail heading to Oxo and skiing it down (around 12). 

…

reports.title: Grandbaby Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Extremely good conditions on the south end of Bow Peak yesterday. Some of the best snow i've skiied in a long time, and great stability. 

Dug several pits over the course of two days here and could not find any significant layers, and could not get a failure down 1m or so. Some wind slab in the couloir, but no more than 3-4" and generally scattered, not widespread. No wind effect to speak …

reports.title: Skier triggered size 1.5 avalanche on Bow Peak
reports.comment: avalanche: Parks Visitor Safety responded to a skier accidental, size 1.5 avalanche on Bow Peak that resulted in minor injuries. It appears to be a wind slab that failed as the group crossed the slope.

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Skied Crystal Ridge from 2520m. 15-20cm low density HST overlies March 21st crust present to 2400m. Dug at 2340 SW (2 profiles), Jan24 dn 85-90, CTN x 2, ECTX x 2.

reports.title: West bow peak
reports.comment:
quick: Skied west bow/peyto trees. 2000m-2350m. 320cmHS @ 2290m. minor wind skin at TL and above, L gusting M West winds. 
clear -> broken Sky. 
Results - CTM 17 RP down 112 on Rounding F sz 1. (suspected Jan24)
CTM 15 (RP) down 65 on F sz 1. (Mar 21)
Observed the Crown of a previous sz 3 Avalanche on NW ridge of West bow. large cornices along ridge top. 

Great quality skiing.

reports.title: Observation Subpeak SW Shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Observed wind effect at 2000m 

20cm of low density snow at treeline and below treeline / weather: No rainfall / snowpack: Other test results:
CTH 23(RP) dn 24cm
CTH 27(SP) dn 90cm

reports.title: Bow hut
reports.comment:
quick: First, thank you to the highway crew for opening up the road. It's the most snow I have seen on the parkway for a while. 

There were really strong winds blowing east "and" west all morning with a lot of blowing snow at ridge top. On the glacier above the hut, I probed 285 cm @2700m. 
Wind affected snow everywhere except in sheltered areas but still enjoyable skiing. 

It was the first time…

reports.title: Wapta Trip, College of the Rockies Golden Campus, Backcountry Travel 2 (March 29-April 2)
reports.comment: avalanche: This Na originated from class 5 terrain and ran onto the moraine below, no pictures due to low visibility. / weather: High of -5°C, low of -17°C, mod winds from the SW (March 29), switch from NW on March 30, light winds on remainder of trip. Trace of new snow. Pleasant weather for the trip. / snowpack: 260-480 HS on the Icefield. 20cm F, progressive snowpack, turns to pencil in a meter.…

reports.title: Ramp Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Skied Ramp Peak on Friday. There’s a good track leading up from the road to the bowl above Mosquito Creek Campground, so travel was fast. On the alpine slopes of the peak the snow was very wind hardened, leading us to bootpack the last 200m. Ski crampons would help immensely. 
There was evidence of the large avy cycle. The N aspect of Noseeum slide but didn’t reach the skin track. Picture i…

reports.title: Flower/dogleg combo
reports.comment: quick: Did a lap of flower couloir followed by dogleg couloir this morning. Skiing conditions in both were excellent. Flower is likely skied out by now as we witnessed 8 people ski the line including ourselves. As we made our way back to the parking lot the snow quickly changed to dense heavy slush at tree line. Took advantage and had a quick snowball fight. Overall great day!

reports.title: Peyto April 3-6
reports.comment: quick: 4 days at Peyto hut, entered via Peyto lake, the normal pullout wasn't plowed so we descended from bow summit. Limited visibility most days with winds and light snow filling tracks quickly and creating wind effect. Huge cornices all over the place with evidence of failures pulling out slabs on Habel, Rhonda, and Baker. Skied, Habel north Bowl, Habel ridge, Tilley, and Peyto toe. Mostly clea…

reports.title: Crowfoot
reports.comment:
quick: -9C @8am Bow Lake Parking

Travel through the trees and canyon was quick and easy in the morning. Not too many spots with running water yet. We didn’t get to the top of the canyon for the standard (summer?) route before skinning out into the trees towards our goal of getting to the saddle under Crowfoot. We travelled on the series of shelves to get the scenic view of the ice field. There wa…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr
reports.comment: quick: Jimmy Jr Peak 2026-04-11. Started at sunrise, a solid freeze down low -7c at the parking lot. Skinning up the gully was icy and slippery, ski crampons were helpful. In the alpine, the crust wasn't as thick so skinning was very challenging as ski crampons wouldn't bite well, we ended up just booting straight up the final 300m instead. It took a while to warm up so we took our sweet time on t…

reports.title: Oxo/Puzzle
reports.comment:
quick: Our group dug 3 pits at 2300m.
0-3cm ice crust
3-25cm moist round crystals (4 fingers)
25-50cm rounds (pencil)
Thin ice layer
50-100cm facets (fist)
One pit had PWL still apparent at 70cm, NE facing slope.

3 compression tests showed:
No reaction
M11, resistive planar collapse at 8-10cm
H27, resistive planar at 50cm

Turned
All
Moist
eARly
Afternoon

This was part of AST2 course with Alpine…

reports.title: Hidden Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Skinned up right side of the creek through trees on an existing up track. We continued up to the back of the bowl, staying on the centre ridge. 

Snow was hard in the morning with a ~3cm crust, topped with a 1cm dusting of snow from last night. 

Wet slide remnants were see on the sides of the bowl. 

Headed down around noon. 

Had some ok turns down through the bowl on the crust. Skied out…

reports.title: Bow Peak
reports.comment: quick: Cold day to start out with a few clouds but turned into a very sunny day with a little wind and got much warmer in the afternoon. Snow was getting significantly heavy and sticky in the afternoon but there were still some good sections above 2300m. Saw a size one avalanche from a day or two ago on the way up to Bow Peak. / avalanche: Bootpacker triggered avalanche see incident tab. / inciden…

reports.title: Mt. Patterson Wind slab
reports.comment: avalanche: Remote triggered a size 2 windslab while traversing on a bench above this unsupported, convex feature. Didnt even realize we triggered anything until we got lower! Entire south face was very wind affected. It seems like winds were blowing both uphill from the cauldron area and off the summit ridge in the opposite direction! We also encountered stubborn windslab on the bootpack up into t…

reports.title: Gordon
reports.comment: quick: Bow lake made some interesting sounds on the morning approach, and with the afternoon slush we took the lakeshore trail on our way back. Travel in the canyon is good, ski crampons were almost mandatory in the morning. Trail might need to be rerouted in a couple places, bridges are falling apart fast. Travel on the icefield was perfect, fast in the morning, soft in the afternoon. Probed 300c…

reports.title: East face of Baker and Mt Habel N ramp
reports.comment:
quick: Travel down to Peyto lake is pretty horrible but it still manageable the snow that we had on our travel in Thursday has completely melted out Friday afternoon on our way back to the car. The summer trail skin track has also melted out so a lot of hiking is required to get up to the toe of the glacier. 
Thursday CLR skies all day, with a good overnight refreeze making for somewhat fast trave…

reports.title: Observation Subpeak
reports.comment:
quick: Good freeze overnight but soft enough for easy skinning.  Dropped the north glacier at 11am with perfect corn skiing, smooth as can be.  Descended the mother's Day couloir below the glacier down to 2350m where it got steeper and became isothermic from the morning sun. 0c at 2950m but 11c at the car at 330pm

West aspect are shallow from the winters wind and are more susceptible to slab aval…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr
reports.comment:
quick: -1 amazing radiative freeze at the road at 6am.  The creek is open and you can cross it at its month behind the lodge.  We used ski crampons through the trees untill the sun was on the slopes for 30 minutes.  Partially sliped into some wells going up through the trees.   

A couple thousand calories short and a couple hours short of sleep, and recovering from the flu brought me to a state o…

reports.title: 5th Winter!
reports.comment:
quick: Rode the paths just north of Jimmy jr bowl. Easy valley crossing with gumboots.

10cm new valley bottom, maybe 18 at the top. Stayed sub zero, no need for skin wax. Constant snow all day but only a little accumulation. Surface froze pretty well prior to new snow so not bonding that well, crampons required on steeper slopes. Could still feel crust, not quite enough for face shots, hopefully …

reports.title: Jimmy Junior
reports.comment:
avalanche: A group of 4 skied Jimmy Junior, 15cm-ish of new snow last 24 hours.
Descended SE on the first half with great skiing and good stability, stopped and regrouped midway.  The next pitch @ ~2500m the first skier triggered a small sluff of fresh loose wet overtop of an ice crust which built momentum and pulled the skier down, they were able to stay on top but slid ~350m and over a small cli…

reports.comment:
avalanche: A group of 4 skied Jimmy Junior, 15cm-ish of new snow last 24 hours.
Descended SE on the first half with great skiing and good stability, stopped and regrouped midway.  The next pitch @ ~2500m the first skier triggered a small sluff of fresh loose wet overtop of an ice crust which built momentum and pulled the skier down, they were able to stay on top but slid ~350m and over a small cli…

reports.title: May 31st Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: True spring variable conditions. Saturday we skied the south chutes, partly cloudy, warm slushy snowpack by noon. Sunday stormy and foggy. Skied dog leg with plenty of snow base available. About 10mm of rain overnight changing to 2-3cm of fresh snow continuously falling throughout the day. Could skin up from the parking lot but beginning to get patchy.
